record.original_question: Characterize the numerical semigroups that can be expressed as quotients of complete intersection numerical semigroups by a positive integer.

evidence.quote: We raise the following questions. What semigroups can be expressed as the quotient of a complete intersection by a positive integer?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A numerical semigroup is a subset $S \subseteq \mathbb{N} = \{0,1,2,\dots\}$ that is closed under addition, contains $0$, and has finite complement in $\mathbb{N}$ (equivalently, $\gcd(S) = 1$). Every numerical semigroup admits a unique minimal system of generators $\{n_1,\dots,n_e\}$, and one writes $S = \langle n_1,\dots,n_eangle$. The integer $e$ is the embedding dimension of $S$.

To each numerical semigroup $S = \langle n_1,\dots,n_eangle$ one associates the semigroup ring $k[S] = k[t^{n_1},\dots,t^{n_e}] \subseteq k[t]$ over a field $k$, presented as $k[x_1,\dots,x_e]/I_S$, where $I_S$ is the kernel of the map sending $x_i \mapsto t^{n_i}$. The semigroup $S$ is called a complete intersection numerical semigroup if the toric ideal $I_S$ can be generated by exactly $e-1$ elements (equivalently, if $k[S]$ is a complete intersection ring).

For a numerical semigroup $T$ and a positive integer $d$, the quotient of $T$ by $d$ is defined to be
$$	frac{T}{d} = \{n \in \mathbb{N} : dn \in T\},$$
which is again a numerical semigroup.

Problem. Characterize the numerical semigroups $S$ that can be expressed as $S = T/d$, where $T$ is a complete intersection numerical semigroup and $d$ is a positive integer.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a numerical semigroups problem list (2013). Subsequent work has addressed related questions—e.g., characterizing numerical semigroups that are quotients of symmetric or of flat semigroups, and constructing examples that are not k-quotients—but a full characterization of those that arise as quotients of complete intersection numerical semigroups by a positive integer does not appear to be available. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: When is a numerical semigroup a quotient?
status_evidence.snippet: Studies when numerical semigroups can be expressed as quotients, including non-trivial examples of semigroups that are not k-quotients.
status_evidence.claim: Related work treats quotient questions for numerical semigroups but does not provide a full characterization for the complete intersection case.

status_evidence.title: Flat semigroups and weighted homogeneous surface singularities
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizes representable numerical semigroups as quotients of flat semigroups.
status_evidence.claim: Recent works characterize quotients of related (e.g., flat) classes, indicating the complete intersection version is still being investigated.

status_evidence.title: Classes of complete intersection numerical semigroups
status_evidence.snippet: Examines several subclasses of complete intersection numerical semigroups and the gluing operation.
status_evidence.claim: Structural studies of complete intersection numerical semigroups continue, but no general quotient characterization is given.
